Rambagh
Palace

A Maharaja's home in Jaipur, since 1835

Scroll to raise the palace
1835

A garden house

It began as a modest pavilion set among gardens beyond Jaipur's old city walls.

Late 1800s

A royal lodge

Later rulers enlarged it into an arcaded guesthouse and hunting lodge for the court.

1925

A Maharaja's home

Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II made Rambagh his residence, crowning it with domes and chhatris.

1957

Doors open to guests

The royal family turned the residence into one of India's first palace hotels.

Today

Lit every evening

Cared for by Taj, the palace still keeps its ceremony, from the lawns to the last lamp on the parapet.

18351800s19251957Today

The jewel of Jaipur

Hand-carved marble latticework, sandstone balustrades and wide Mughal gardens. For nearly two centuries the palace has kept its ceremonial grandeur, and every guest is received the way the court once received its own.

Rooms and suites

Seventy-eight ways to live like royalty

Forty-five rooms and thirty-three suites, each opening onto a garden or courtyard. The grand suites keep the palace's royal character, with a butler on call around the clock.

  • Royal butlerAssigned to every suite
  • Garden or courtyardViews from every room
  • In-room diningServed day and night
  • FamiliesInterconnecting rooms on request
